text: Something just shot out from under the kitchen sink. I was reaching for the dish soap and a dark shape brushed my hand. My heart is slamming against my ribs. I'm standing on a chair now, clutching the tea towel, and I genuinely cannot make my legs climb down.

The ladder just lurched sideways while I was clipping the hedge. I've grabbed the gutter and now I'm frozen up here, knuckles white, not breathing. Every tiny wobble shoots straight through my stomach. Don't look down. Don't look down. Why did I think I could do this alone?

The train lights just cut out in the tunnel and the carriage dropped into total black with a screech of brakes. My hand is clamped on the pole so hard it hurts. Somebody gasped behind me. I can hear my own pulse in my ears and I can't see a thing.

I'm gaming late with headphones on and a hand lands on my shoulder out of nowhere. I nearly leap out of the chair. My whole body goes cold and my throat closes up. It's only my brother wanting the charger, but my hands are still jittering on the controller.

Don't move. Seriously, don't move. There's a wasp the size of my thumb on your collar. No, no, stop flapping! Oh no, it's in my hair now. Get it out, get it out, please, I can feel it buzzing right by my ear!

Whoa, whoa, is that dog on a lead? It's charging straight at us! Get behind the bench, quick. My heart is going a million miles an hour. Okay, okay, the owner's grabbed it. I honestly thought it was going to knock me flat.

Did you hear that? That crack was right on top of us! The whole window rattled. Grab the cat and come away from the glass, please. I nearly dropped the pan. My legs have gone to jelly and I keep flinching every time the sky flashes.

Mum, I'm in the lift at work and it just dropped a few feet and jolted to a stop between floors. Lights flickering. I pressed the alarm and nothing's happened yet. Please call me. My hands are shaking so much I can barely type this.

Bro there is a HUGE spider on the bathroom ceiling right above the shower and it just moved. I'm standing in the hallway in a towel with my heart pounding. I am not going back in there. Can you come over right now and deal with it??

The oil just went up in a whoosh of flame on the hob!! I slammed the lid on and switched it off. It's out but I'm jittering all over and the smoke alarm is screaming. Can you come downstairs? I don't want to be in the kitchen by myself right now.

Walking home from the bus tonight a fox shrieked in the hedge right beside me and I swear I jumped out of my skin. Twenty minutes later my heart is still thudding and I keep flinching at every rustle outside the window.

At practice today a cricket ball came off the bat straight at my face and missed by an inch. I heard it whistle past my ear. I just stood there, frozen, mouth open, unable to breathe for a second. My chest is still tight thinking about it.

He just presented my slides in the meeting as his own work. My slides. The ones I stayed late on Thursday to finish. He didn't even change the font. My face is burning and my jaw is clenched so tight it aches. I am not letting this go.

That driver just cut across two lanes, nearly clipped my bike, then leaned on the horn at ME. At me! I'm gripping the handlebars so hard my knuckles have gone white. Every part of me wants to catch him at the next light and tell him exactly what I think.

Someone ate the lasagne I labelled with my name and the date. Took the whole portion and left the dish in the sink, unwashed. I spent two hours making that. I'm standing in the office kitchen with my teeth clenched, about to email the entire floor.

My teammate just quit mid-match on purpose because he wasn't top scorer, and now we all lose ranked points for his tantrum. I was one round from promotion. I smacked the desk so hard my drink jumped. Unbelievable. Reported, blocked, done.

No. You do not get to cancel on me twenty minutes before kick off when I paid for your ticket. I bought it in July! I've been standing at the gate in the rain. You knew all week you had this other thing. Don't you dare tell me to relax.

Excuse me, did you just tip your grass cuttings over the fence onto my tomatoes? I watched you do it! I planted those in April. Now half of them are flattened under a heap of your clippings. Get them off. Right now.

You told me it was fixed. I paid eighty pounds and walked out of here an hour ago, and the screen is already black again. Don't shrug at me. I want my money back or a working phone, today, not next week.

Who touched my desk?? I come back from lunch and my monitor is unplugged, my notes are in the recycling bin, and someone's sitting in my chair. I asked yesterday, politely, that nobody move my things. This is out of order. I want an answer now.

You told Dad about my exam results before I could. I specifically asked you to let me tell him myself. You promised! Now he's ringing me already disappointed and I never got the chance to explain. Thanks a lot. Seriously, thanks a lot.

The landlord let himself into my flat while I was at work, no notice at all. I got home to the thermostat changed and muddy bootprints across my rug. That is not okay. I'm ringing him the second I finish typing this.

Ref gave a penalty against us for a dive the whole ground could see. The whole ground! Lost one nil. I shouted myself hoarse and booted a crisp packet across the car park on the way out. Still seething. Going to bed before I write anything worse.

The airline sold my seat twice and handed it to someone else at the gate. They just shrugged and said the next flight was tomorrow. I stood there with my voice rising and my face hot while the agent kept typing. Absolute nerve.

The restructure announcement is supposedly next month and nobody knows what it means for our team. Could be nothing. Could be everything. I keep rereading old emails for clues and refreshing the intranet. I've checked my inbox eleven times since lunch and I can't settle into a single task.

What if the scholarship goes to someone else, and then the rent goes up, and then I can't afford second year? I know I'm spiralling. Results aren't due until March. But my brain keeps running every version where it all goes sideways, and none where it doesn't.

They're forecasting frost again next week and the seedlings are only just through. If they go, the whole summer plan goes with them. I keep checking the app, then checking again, as if the numbers will change. My stomach has been tight all evening over a tray of tomatoes.

Mum hasn't answered her phone since this morning, which is probably just her garden club. Probably. Still, my mind keeps drifting to the dodgy boiler and that loose stair carpet. I've typed and deleted three messages. I can't focus on this spreadsheet at all.

Do you think the move will actually go through? The buyers keep asking for more time, the mortgage offer expires next month, and if anything slips we're stuck paying for two places. I keep lying awake doing the numbers. Tell me honestly, am I overthinking it?

She's barely touched her food since we moved, and she spends all day hiding under the bed. I know cats are fussy. I just can't stop wondering if she's ever going to settle here, or if I've wrecked her whole routine by dragging her across the city.

If we drop another point this weekend we probably miss the playoffs, and then the sponsor might pull out, and then who knows if there's even a team next season. I keep going over the fixtures in my head at night. Does that sound mad to you?

Has anyone heard anything about the budget for next quarter? Finance has gone quiet and our project wasn't on the agenda. Probably fine, but I keep wondering whether we'll still be funded in spring. Sorry for the random ping, it's been sitting on my mind all day.

Hey, did you hear back about the flat? The agent hasn't replied to me and there were loads of people at the viewing. I keep thinking if we don't get this one we're back to square one, and our lease ends in six weeks. Let me know anything at all.

Quick one: did the parcel with Grandma's birthday present arrive? Tracking has said 'in transit' for four days now. If it's lost I don't know what else I can get to her in time. I keep refreshing the page like that will somehow help.

Couldn't sleep again. Ran through everything: the deadline, the car's MOT, whether the new job will even last past probation. None of it is happening tonight, but the list kept looping until three. Made tea at 3am. Still no answers.

The weather apps can't agree about Saturday and the whole garden party depends on it. Rain means forty people squeezed into our small flat. Checked the forecast all day. Spent the evening drafting backup plans for the backup plans.

Rain is ticking gently on the shed roof and I'm in no hurry at all. The seed trays can wait. I've got a mug of tea warming my hands and nothing on the list that can't be done tomorrow. My shoulders have finally dropped. I'm just listening.

Train delayed forty minutes. Fine. I find a seat on the platform bench, put my earphones in, and watch the pigeons squabble over a crust. Nothing I do will make it come faster, so there's no point clenching about it. I breathe slowly and wait.

Sunday morning, nothing planned. I'm stirring the porridge in slow circles while the radio murmurs in the other room. Steam curls up past the window. My breathing has slowed to the pace of the spoon. Nowhere I need to be for hours.

The phone has frozen on the update screen again. Okay. I set it face down on the table, make a coffee, and give it ten minutes. If it needs a reset, I'll do a reset. Everything important is backed up. There's no rush, and nothing here can't be sorted.

Okay, let's slow down for a second. The client moved the deadline, yes, but we still have two full days and most of the work is done. Let's list what's left, split it between us, and take it one thing at a time. We'll be fine.

Shh, it's alright, buddy. It's just the fireworks over the river. Come here, lie down next to me. That's it. Nice slow breaths. We'll sit right here on the rug with the telly low until they finish. You're safe, I've got you.

Two nil down at half time isn't the end of anything. Drink some water, sit down, breathe. We know how to play this team. Keep the ball, be patient, and the chances will come. No shouting, no rushing. Just our game, one pass at a time.

No problem at all about running late. I'm at the café by the window with a book and a pot of tea, perfectly settled. Take your time, drive carefully, and I'll be right here whenever you arrive. Honestly, it's a nice excuse to sit still.

Hi Mum, got your voicemail. The flight is just delayed, nothing more. I've got snacks, a charger and a comfy corner seat by the gate. I'll text when we board. Go to bed, honestly, there's nothing to wait up for. All fine on my end.

Hey, saw your message about the exam. You've done the revision, you know the material. Tonight just have a proper dinner, lay out your pens, and get a good night's sleep. Whatever comes up tomorrow, you'll take it steadily. Talk after?

Spent the evening weeding the bottom bed while the light faded. No phone, no podcast, just the trowel and a blackbird on the fence. My mind went quiet in a way it hasn't for weeks. Slept straight through.

Long walk by the lake after work. The water was flat and grey, barely moving. Sat on the bench for a while doing nothing at all. Came home slowly, cooked something simple, and left the dishes until morning without a second thought.

Three percent battery, no charger, and my boarding pass is only on this phone. I've asked four cafés for a socket and every single one is taken. If it goes flat, I don't get on the plane. I'm pacing the terminal begging strangers, holding the phone like it might somehow last.

Essay due at nine, it's half four in the morning, and I'm still two thousand words short. I've tried everything: coffee, cold water on my face, bullet points just to get something down. Please, brain, give me one more paragraph. Just one more. Anything at all.

I've turned out every pocket and every bag twice. The keys are not here. The locksmith can't come until tomorrow, my phone is nearly flat, and it's starting to pour. I'm on my knees peering under the car with the torch, pleading with them to be there.

The presentation file won't open. Corrupted, it says. The client is in the lobby, the meeting starts in six minutes, and the backup is on the laptop I left at home. I'm clicking everything, recovering old versions, anything. Please, just one version that opens.

Please, I'm begging you, can you hold the bus for one minute? My daughter is running up the hill right now with her bag, she's right there, look. This is the last one tonight. Please, just thirty seconds. I'll pay for both of us, whatever it takes.

Have you seen a small grey cat with a white chest? She slipped out this morning and she's never been outside before. I've knocked on every door on this street. Could I check your shed, please? Just a quick look. I can't go home without her.

Ref, please, just let me grab my gloves from the car, it's two minutes! I'm the only keeper we've got today. If I can't play we forfeit, and that's us relegated. Please. I'll sprint the whole way. I'll be back before kick off, I promise.

Does ANYONE on this floor have a USB-C charger I could borrow for ten minutes?? Laptop is on 1% and I'm presenting to the board at two. I will buy you lunch for a week. Please reply, I'm literally going desk to desk asking people.

Mum please pick up. I'm at the airport and my passport is still on the kitchen table. Check-in closes in fifty minutes. Is there ANY chance you or Dad can drive it over right now? I'll pay for petrol, anything. Please call me back the second you see this.

Emergency!! Dinner party in an hour and the oven has just stopped heating. Twelve people coming. Can I please, please borrow yours? I'll bring the trays over now and you won't even notice I'm there. I have no other option, I'm begging.

Spent the whole day trying to reach the bank about the frozen card. Rent is due tomorrow. On hold for two hours, cut off twice, rang again. Ended up pleading with a recorded voice. Still nothing. Going to queue outside the branch before it opens.

Tickets for the final sold out in four minutes. I sat refreshing on three devices, got my cousin trying on his account too, kept hammering the button. Error after error. Tonight I've emailed every reseller I can find. I have to be there. I have to.

The first tomatoes are finally turning red and I can't stop going out to look at them! I've already planned three sauces, a salsa and a salad. Tomorrow I'm building a second raised bed. The seed catalogue is open on the table and I want everything in it.

The expansion drops at midnight and I've cleared the whole weekend. Snacks ready, headset charged, notes on every new class printed out. I've watched the trailer about forty times and I keep pausing to point at tiny details. This is going to be incredible.

Right, sourdough attempt number one starts now! The starter's bubbling, the flour's weighed, and I've watched every tutorial going. I'm baking every single weekend from here on. Then focaccia, then bagels, maybe croissants by Christmas. Let's go!

The new running club starts Tuesday and I've already bought the shoes, a reflective vest and a little armband for my phone. I've mapped three routes. I want a 10k by spring, then maybe a half marathon. Honestly, I'd go out tonight if I could.

Wait, can I take this project? Please? I've been itching to try the new design tool, and I already sketched a few layouts on the train this morning. Look, look at this one. I could have a first draft by Thursday. I'm totally up for it!

Grandad, guess what! I've booked us the fishing trip for your birthday, the boat, the guide, everything. Two whole days on the lake! I've already sorted the flasks and the folding chairs. You have to come. It's going to be brilliant!

Have you seen the module list for next term? Astronomy! Actual astronomy, with the telescope on the roof! I'm signing up first thing tomorrow. We should do it together. Imagine mapping a whole constellation at midnight. Come on, say yes!

Team!! Just booked the five-a-side pitch for every Thursday from next month. Who's in? I'll bring the bibs and cones. Let's get a proper squad going, maybe even enter the league in spring. Reply with a thumbs up, I want names by Friday!!

The puppy is coming home SATURDAY!! I've bought the bed, the toys, a tiny raincoat, and read three books on training. Can you come and meet her? I've already planned a walk route through the park. I literally can't wait!!

Just got a plot at the community allotment!! Number 14, right by the apple tree. I'm going down Sunday with a spade and a flask. Want to share it with me? Pumpkins, beans, strawberries, everything. I've already started a planting spreadsheet.

The keyboard arrived today and I spent four hours learning chords. Fingers aching, but I've already ordered a beginner's songbook and signed up for Thursday lessons. Want to play my favourite album start to finish by summer. Can't wait for tomorrow.

First climbing session done! Made it halfway up the yellow wall. I've booked five more classes, borrowed my sister's chalk bag, and found a bouldering gym near work. Going again Wednesday. Maybe Thursday too. Maybe every day.

And the phone has restarted itself again. Fourth time today, right in the middle of typing a message. Of course. I've updated it, reset it, cleared the cache, done every single thing the forums said. Here we go, watching the logo spin. Again.

The cat knocks the pen off the desk. I put it back. She knocks it off. I put it back. She looks me dead in the eye and knocks it off. This has happened every morning for a month. I'm just going to stop owning pens.

Third meeting this week to decide the colour of one button. Blue was agreed on Monday. Green on Tuesday. Now someone wants to revisit blue. I'm rubbing my temples while the same slides go round in circles. Can we please, please just pick one?

Signal failure at the same junction. Again. Every single Monday it's the same announcement, the same apology, the same forty minutes on this platform. I could recite it along with them. I've stopped even checking the board. I just lean on the pillar and wait.

How many times do I have to say it? Shoes go on the rack, not in the middle of the hallway. I've tripped over these trainers three times today. Three! I'm not asking for much. Just the rack. It's right there. Please.

Mate, for the tenth time, the washing up doesn't do itself. I've asked nicely, I've made a rota, I've stuck a note on the fridge. And there's still a pan from Tuesday in the sink. I'm honestly running out of ways to say this.

Yes, I've already turned it off and on again. Yes, I checked the cables. Yes, the light is green. I told the last three people exactly this. No, please don't put me on hold again. I've been on this call for an hour.

Hi Dave, resending the invoice once more, as attached to my emails on the 3rd, the 10th and the 17th. Same invoice, same amount, same bank details. Could you confirm you've actually received it this time? Thanks. Again.

Dad, the wifi password is still on the sticky note on the fridge, where I left it last week, and the week before. You don't need to reset the router. Please don't reset the router again. I'll come round Sunday and show you. For the fourth time.

Guys, this group chat is for the football fixtures, not memes. I've said it every week this season. I've just scrolled past two hundred cat videos to find out where Saturday's game is. Can someone please just tell me the pitch number?
Neighbour's car alarm went off at six again. Third morning in a row. I've left two polite notes already. Lay there staring at the ceiling waiting for it to stop. It never stops quickly. Never.

Rewrote the report for the fifth time tonight after another round of small tweaks. Each round undoes the last one, so we're basically back at version one. Shut the laptop, put the kettle on, and muttered at it for a while.

The forecast says the frost arrives Thursday night, and every seedling I've raised since March is still out in the open beds. I keep picturing the tomatoes blackened and limp by Friday morning. Three days to go and I already know I won't sleep that night, listening for the wind to drop.

The restructure email said 'more details on Monday.' That's it. Five words and a whole weekend to fill in the rest. I keep running through which teams would be merged first, and ours is the obvious one. Every time my phone buzzes I flinch before I even look at it.

Results go up on the portal at nine tomorrow. I've already worked out that if I missed the pass mark in statistics, I'd have to resit in August and lose the internship. I keep refreshing a page that won't change until morning, just in case it does.

The update is downloading and the forum is full of people saying it wiped their save files. Two hundred hours on that farm. I could stop it, but then the game won't launch at all. I'm sitting here watching the bar creep toward a hundred percent like it's counting down to something.

Dad, when the garage calls back about the gearbox, just tell me the number straight away, okay? Don't build up to it. I've been adding up my savings all week and I already know it won't cover the big repair. If it's that one, I don't know how I get to work next month.

Can we not check the league table yet? If we lose on Sunday and they win, we go down, and the whole club drops a division. I can't even think about a season in that lower league. Just, let's not look until after the match. Please.

So the client wants to see the full demo on Friday, live, with their board watching. You know the export still crashes about one time in five. I keep imagining it freezing right as their director leans in. What do we do if it goes wrong on the big screen?

hey did you see the email from the landlord? 'inspection next thursday, all rooms.' the stain on the carpet in my room is NOT coming out and the deposit is basically all my savings. i keep thinking they'll keep the whole thing. can you look at it with me tonight?

Hi Priya, just a heads up before the quarterly numbers go out. Mine are well below target and I suspect the review on the 14th won't go the way I'd like. I'm already rehearsing what I'll say if they bring up the team change. Could we talk beforehand? I'd rather not walk in blind.

the weather app now says the storm hits saturday morning, right when we're meant to be on the ferry. if they cancel it we miss the wedding rehearsal. if they don't cancel it... i don't even want to think about that crossing. checking again every hour.
Interview is in four days. Tonight I lay awake listing every question I could freeze on. By two a.m. I had already pictured the long silence, the polite nod, the email that starts 'unfortunately'.

Still no word from the scholarship office. The rent is due on the first, and without the grant I don't know where that money comes from. Each day the inbox stays empty, the first of the month gets closer.

Another grey morning, the fourth this week. The bus is late again and the windows are fogged so you can't even see the street. Same desk waiting, same inbox, same nothing. I can't remember the last time a Monday felt like it was going anywhere. Next week will probably be just like this one.

The slugs got the lettuces overnight, every single one. I could replant, but what's the point? They'll be back, the rain isn't stopping, and the season's half over anyway. The whole plot looks like a muddy patch someone forgot about. Maybe that's all it is now.

Six weeks of revision and the practice paper still came back at forty percent. I look at the stack of notes and it just feels like a wall. Everyone else seems to get it. I'll sit the real exam, I'll probably get the same mark, and then it'll be summer and nothing will have changed.

We've lost eleven in a row. I still put the shirt on every Saturday out of habit, but I already know how it ends. Two nil down by half time, the stands emptying, the long drive home in the rain. Next season won't be any different. It never is.

Honestly, I don't see the point in redoing the kitchen plan again. The budget won't stretch, the landlord won't agree, and by the time we save enough the prices will have gone up anyway. Let's just leave it how it is. It's always going to be a bit dark and cramped in here.

Did you look outside? Rain until Thursday, then more rain. The washing won't dry, the heating's broken, and the repair guy can't come until next month. I think this whole winter is just going to be this. Wet socks and cold toast and staring at the wall.

No, I'm not coming to the quiz this week. We come last every time, and then everyone goes home a bit flat. Same questions we don't know, same team that beats us, same long walk back in the dark. I'd rather just stay in.

the job board's been empty for weeks. applied to three more today but i'm not expecting anything. nobody ever writes back. starting to think this is just how it's going to be for a long while. anyway how's your week

Hi all, just to confirm the project is delayed again, now until spring. I'm not sure spring will hold either, honestly. Every time we fix one thing, two more turn up. I'll keep sending updates, but I wouldn't plan anything around a date for now.

phone screen cracked again. third time this year. can't afford a new one so i guess i'm living with a spiderweb across everything till next christmas at least. the sky outside is the same flat grey as the crack. what a year.
Dark by four again. Walked home under the same flat sky, heated the same soup. The days are only getting shorter from here, and there's nothing on the calendar until March but bills and early nights.
The cat won't come out from under the bed and I don't blame her. Rain on the window all day, the radiator ticking, the job applications going nowhere. I can't picture any of this lifting soon.

She stayed after her shift for two hours just to walk me through the new system, and never once made me feel slow. I'd have been lost all week without that. I keep thinking about how easily she could have gone home. I owe her a coffee. Honestly, I owe her a lot more than that.

My neighbour watered my whole garden for the ten days I was away, without being asked, even the fussy pots by the shed. I came back and the beans were climbing the canes. I don't know how I'll ever repay that, but I'm going to try, starting with a basket of whatever ripens first.

The teammate who swapped shifts so I could make my sister's graduation didn't have to. He gave up his own Saturday for it. I sat in that hall and watched her cross the stage, and the whole time I kept thinking, I'm only here because of him.

Some stranger in the lobby spent forty minutes teaching me how to block properly, then sent me his controller settings. No reason, he just saw I was struggling. I won my first ranked match tonight with his layout. I don't even know his real name, but I'll never forget that gamertag.

Grandma, you didn't have to post me that whole box of recipes. I read every card last night, the stains and the little notes in the margins and everything. I made your lentil soup today and it tasted like your kitchen. Thank you. Really. That box means more to me than anything I own.

Coach, I just wanted to say, you could've dropped me after that first season. I was slow and I missed every tackle. You kept me on, gave me extra drills, stayed late with me. Today I started in the final. That's on you as much as me.

You found my phone on the seat? Oh my word, everything's on there, my tickets, my photos, my mum's number. You ran all the way down the platform with it? Please, let me at least buy you a tea. I can't tell you what this means.

just got home and saw you'd fixed the leaky tap AND left dinner in the fridge. i've had the worst week and i genuinely don't know what i did to deserve you as a flatmate. thank you thank you thank you. i'm doing the bins for a month.

Dear Mr Okafor, I wanted to write properly to thank you for the reference. I got the place on the course this morning, and the admissions tutor mentioned your letter specifically. You took time you didn't have to vouch for me, and I won't forget it.
you remembered i had my driving test today and texted at 7am to wish me luck. nobody else did. passed by the way!! that message honestly got me through the parallel parking. i owe you big time

The whole office chipped in to cover my train fare home when my card got blocked. Nobody made a fuss, they just did it. I keep going over it in my head tonight, feeling lucky to sit among these people.

Dad drove three hours to help me move flats and refused to take petrol money. He carried the sofa up four floors and then cooked for us. I don't say it enough. I'm writing it here so I at least say it somewhere: thank you.

I ate the last slice of his birthday cake from the fridge at midnight and told myself he'd forgotten it was there. He hadn't. He opened the box this morning and just went quiet. I should have said something straight away. Now it's been six hours and every minute makes it harder to admit.

Mum rang three times on Sunday and I let every call go to voicemail because I was in the middle of a match. Three times. She only wanted to tell me the roses had come out. I keep replaying her little 'ring me when you can, sweetheart' and picturing her sitting by the phone.

In the meeting I let them think the missed deadline was the design team's fault. It wasn't. I sat on the files for a week. Jess got the hard questions and I just nodded along. She caught my eye once, and I looked down at my notes. I can't stop seeing that.

The dog sat by the door the whole time I was out, my neighbour said. I'd promised him a long walk this morning and then went to brunch instead. Now he's lying with his chin on my shoe, not even sulking, just glad I'm back. That almost makes it worse.

Tom, I need to tell you something about your bike. I borrowed it last week and scraped the frame against a wall. I painted over it thinking you wouldn't notice. That was a rotten thing to do. I'll pay for a proper respray, whatever it costs. I'm really sorry.

Sorry, I know I said I'd do my slides for the group project and I just... didn't. You all stayed up finishing them, and then I stood up and presented as if I'd helped. It's been sitting on me all week. Next one, I'll do the whole write-up myself.

Grandad, I'm sorry I missed your call on your birthday. I was out with friends and kept saying I'd ring back, and then it was midnight. You waited up, didn't you. I should've just stepped outside for five minutes. Can I come round Saturday and make it up to you?

hey i owe you an apology. i told everyone in the group chat your idea for the trip was boring before you'd even finished explaining it. it was a cheap shot and i saw your replies go quiet after. i was wrong. can i buy you lunch and actually listen this time?

Hi Sam, I've realised I used your analysis in my report to the director without crediting you. She praised it in front of everyone and I just accepted it. That wasn't fair to you at all. I'm sending her a correction this morning with your name on it.

i completely forgot your recital tonight. i'd written it down and everything. i'm sitting here looking at the photos from everyone else who came and i want to crawl under a rock. you practised for months. i'm so sorry. tell me when you play next and i'll be in the front row.
Snapped at the new intern for a mistake that was really down to my bad instructions. He apologised to me. I let him. Lay in bed replaying his face and the way he said 'it won't happen again.'
Promised the kids pancakes this morning, then slept through the alarm and handed them cereal. They didn't complain once. Small thing, I know, but it's been nagging at me all day.

The sun's out, the bread actually rose this time, and the whole flat smells like a bakery. I've got music on and I'm dancing around the kitchen in my socks. Nothing big happened. It's just one of those days where everything clicks and I can't stop humming.

First ripe strawberry of the year, still warm from the sun. I ate it right there in the garden, standing in the dirt in my slippers. The neighbour's kid waved from over the fence and I waved back like a fool. This is the best Saturday I've had in ages.

We won! Last minute, a header off the corner, and the whole bench ran onto the pitch. My voice is gone from shouting. I'm on the train home with mud on my knees and a grin I can't wipe off. What a day.

Finally beat the last boss after two weeks of trying. The credits are rolling and I'm just sitting here with the controller in my lap, beaming at the screen. My sister came in to see what the yelling was about and now she's doing a victory dance with me.

Guess what, they said yes! The flat with the big window and the balcony, it's ours from the first. We can finally have that herb garden you keep talking about. I couldn't wait to tell you, I ran the whole way here from the agent's office.

Mum, can you hear me? Everyone's here, all of us at the same table for the first time in years. Dad's carving, the kids are making a racket, Aunt Sita brought her famous dumplings. I just wanted you on speaker so you could hear it. It's perfect.

Look at him! The puppy's finally figured out the stairs. Every step, he does this little hop and then looks back at us like he's the cleverest dog alive. I can't stop watching. Honestly, this is the best thing I've seen all week.
PASSED!!!! all four modules, even stats!!! i'm literally jumping around on the library steps right now. dinner tonight, my treat, everyone's invited. best day of the whole year by miles

Hi team, just a quick note to say the launch went perfectly. Zero bugs, and the client called it the smoothest release they've ever had. I'm sitting here with a coffee and a ridiculous smile on my face. Cake in the kitchen at three. Well done, every one of you.

the sun came out, i biked to work along the river, got a free pastry because the cafe was celebrating its birthday, and my code ran first try. honestly can't remember a better tuesday. how's yours going?
Spent the whole afternoon on the allotment with Dad, planting garlic and swapping silly stories. Came home sunburnt and muddy and humming. Days like this are the ones I want to keep.
Snow day! The office closed, and the street turned into one big sledging hill. Built a lopsided snowman with the neighbours' kids and drank hot chocolate on the step. Best Wednesday in memory.

The seedlings finally pushed through the soil this morning, tiny green hooks after two weeks of nothing. If the weather holds, there might actually be tomatoes by July. I'm already picturing the window box full. Maybe this year the garden really works out.

The second interview went better than the first. They asked when I could start, which has to mean something, right? I'm trying not to plan the commute yet, but I've already looked up the train times twice. Things could really turn around this month.

Down to two seconds off the qualifying time. Three months ago I was eight seconds off. If I keep up the morning swims, I could be there by the regional meet. For the first time the number feels reachable, not just a fantasy.

The mock came back at fifty-eight, up from forty-one. Still not the grade I need, but it's moving, and the topics I drilled are the ones that went right. Six weeks left. If the next block goes the same way, I could actually get the place I applied for.

Okay, so the bank didn't say no. They said come back in three months with six payslips. That's not a rejection, that's a plan. If I keep saving like this, by spring we could be looking at flats with a garden. I really think we're nearly there.

Look, we lost, but did you see the second half? We held them for forty minutes. The passing was the best it's been all season. If we keep training like that, the cup game in two weeks is completely winnable. I mean it. Something's starting to click.

The landlord rang back about the corner unit. He's willing to talk about the rent. Nothing's signed, I know, but imagine it, my own little cafe by spring, your paintings on the walls. It might actually happen this time.

update on the cat: she ate half her dinner tonight and came to sit on the sofa for the first time since we brought her home. still shy but she purred!! i think she's going to settle in fine. give it a week or two

Hi Marta, the client hasn't confirmed yet, but they asked for full pricing and a timeline, which they never do unless they're serious. I'll send it over today. If this lands, we'd have work booked through next summer. Fingers crossed for Friday.
the forecast just changed!! sun on saturday after all. if it holds we can do the picnic at the lake like we planned. i'm keeping the blanket in the car just in case. tell the others not to cancel yet
First day at the new job done. Didn't know anyone, got lost twice, but my manager said the onboarding gets easier by week two. I think this might be the start of something good.
The rose cutting I almost threw out has two new leaves. I'd given up on it in March. Moved it to the sunny sill tonight. Maybe by summer it'll flower.

There he goes again, Marcus, replying all to the team thread just to correct my spreadsheet in public. Fine. Two can play that game. From now on every one of his tickets gets my full attention, every typo, every missed deadline, logged and forwarded. I'm done being polite to someone who has never once been polite back.

I watch her lean over the fence again, eyeing my tomatoes like she owns them. She complained to the council about my compost bin, so she can forget about borrowing my ladder ever again. I'll nod at her across the hedge, sure, but I'm keeping a list, and she's right at the top of it.

Every match this week, same username, same smug little emote after he wins. I've queued into him six times now. I don't even care about the rank anymore. I just want to beat Kestrel99 so badly that he logs off, and then I want to do it again tomorrow, and the day after that.

Jonah's mug is in the sink again, the one with the stupid slogan. I'm not washing it. I'm not washing anything of his ever again. He can eat off the counter for all I care. Six months of him treating me like the cleaner, and he still thinks we're friends. We're not.

No, Dana, you don't get to walk into my meeting and take over the slides. You've undercut me in front of the client twice now. Sit down, keep quiet, and if you've got a problem with how I run my accounts, put it in writing so everyone can see exactly what you're doing.

Don't pass to me, then. Go on, keep hogging the ball like you have all season. But when the coach asks why we lost again, I'm telling him exactly who it was, Ryan. I'm not covering for you anymore, and nobody else on this team will either.

Oh, you're giving cooking advice now? That's rich, coming from you. You've picked apart my lasagne at every single family dinner for ten years. Here's an idea: bring your own next time, and eat it at the far end of the table, well away from me.

Kevin, stop posting in the building group chat about my parking. I've seen your notes on my windscreen and I've kept every single one. If you want to keep this up, carry on, but copies go to the landlord on Monday. Don't knock on my door again. Just don't.

Hi Priya, since you've decided my work isn't worth crediting in the quarterly report, I'll be copying our manager on everything I send you from now on. Every file, every draft, every timestamp. Don't bother replying with a cheery emoji. We both know exactly what you're doing.

Saw you joined the book club, Tom. Interesting choice, given it's my book club. Don't expect anyone there to take your side this time. I've already told them how you behaved at the quiz night. Good luck finding someone who'll sit next to you.

Tuesday. Gareth from accounts again. He 'forgot' to book my room for the third time, and grinned about it. I don't trust a word that man says. Tomorrow I'm making sure everyone sees his numbers before mine. He started this, and I intend to keep it going.

Saturday. The woman at number nine let her dog dig up my bulbs and then told me to get a proper fence. I said nothing. I'm saving it. Every time she parks across my drive from now on, I'm reporting it. She's made her choice and so have I.

She's asleep on the sofa with the cat on her chest, both of them snoring a little. I tuck the blanket over her feet and turn the telly down. I could watch this all evening. Twenty years, and I still get that warm jolt every time she mumbles my name in her sleep.

Gran's hands are dusted with flour up to the wrists, and she's humming that old tune while she rolls the dough. I lean on the counter just to be near her. Every Sunday I tell myself I'll finally learn the recipe, but really I just come for her.

My boy misses the ball completely, spins around, and looks straight at me to check if I saw. I did. I always do. I clap like he's scored in a cup final. He's six and muddy and perfect, and I'd stand in this drizzle every weekend for the rest of my life.

Her train's delayed again, so I'm waiting on the platform with her favourite pastry going cold in its paper bag. I don't mind at all. I keep picturing her face when she spots me. Honestly, these little waits are some of my favourite minutes of the whole week.

Come here, you. No, leave the dishes, I'll do them. You cooked, you sat through my terrible jokes, you remembered my mum's birthday when I didn't. Just sit with me a minute. I don't say it enough, but you're the best thing in every single one of my days.

Dad, I don't care that the line keeps cutting out, keep talking. Tell me about the tomatoes again. I want every detail. I miss hearing you pottering in the kitchen. You know I'm always here for you, right? Ring me whenever you like, even at silly o'clock.

Who's a good girl? You are. Yes, you, with your muddy paws and your one floppy ear. I don't even mind about the sofa. Come on, up you get, there's room for both of us. You're my best mate, you know that? Best mate in the whole world.

Morning, gorgeous. Left you coffee in the flask and a note in your coat pocket. Don't read it on the bus or you'll go all soppy in public. Good luck with the presentation, you'll be brilliant. Can't wait to hear about it tonight. Counting the hours. xx

Just found that photo of us on the beach with the terrible haircuts. Made my whole day. I know we bicker about everything, but you're my favourite person on the planet and I'd fly across the world for you. Call me this weekend? I want to hear your voice.

Dear Sam, Grandad here. Your mum says you've been up late studying. Don't forget to eat something proper. I've put a little money in your account for pizza. Whatever the results are, you'll always be my favourite boy. Write back when you can. All my heart, Grandad.

Sunday. Spent the whole afternoon in the garden with Mum, planting her bulbs. She kept telling me I was doing it wrong and I didn't care one bit. I'd plant a thousand bulbs wrong just to hear her bossing me about. She's my whole world, really.

Wednesday. Ben fixed my bike without being asked and left a sticky note on the saddle: brakes done, ride safe. I've kept the note in my wallet. Eleven years married and he still makes my chest go warm over the smallest things.

Seven minutes until the video interview. I've checked my camera three times and fixed my collar twice. My mouth is so dry. What if the wifi drops right when they ask about my weaknesses? Okay, breathe. Notes on the left, water on the right. Six minutes now.

The ref puts the ball on the spot and steps back, and suddenly my legs feel like jelly. Left corner. I decided left corner this morning. Don't look at the keeper. Don't look at the crowd. My hands won't stop fiddling with my shirt. Just run up and hit it.

I'm standing outside her parents' front door holding flowers and a bottle of wine, and I can't make myself ring the bell. What if I call her dad by the wrong name? What if I knock something over? My palms are sweating straight through the paper. Okay. One, two, three.

The examiner is clipping his pen to the board and I keep wiping my hands on my jeans. Mirror, signal, manoeuvre. I've done this a hundred times with Dad. Why does the gearstick suddenly feel like it belongs to a stranger? Please let me not stall at the first junction.

Can you just listen to my opening one more time before I go up? I keep tripping over the second line. Sorry, my voice is all wobbly. Is my mic on straight? Okay, okay. If I freeze, give me a thumbs up from the back row, alright? Promise me.

Mum, can you sit next to me while the results page loads? I can't look. It's still loading. Oh, it's still loading. My stomach is doing flips. No, don't read it out yet. Wait. Just give me a second. Okay. Okay, now. Actually, no, wait.

First game for the club and I've retied my laces about four times. Do I look alright? My hands are all fidgety. If the coach puts me on in the second half, just shout where you want the ball, yeah? Keep it simple for me. I'll settle once I'm out there.

Presenting to the whole department in 20 mins. I've read my slides so often I could recite them backwards and I still feel like I'm going to forget my own name. If you're free, send me something silly to look at right before I go in. Please.

Okay, about to send the email asking the landlord if we can get a cat. Finger is literally hovering over the send button. What if she says no and then thinks we're trouble? Ugh. Doing it. Doing it now. Text me in five minutes so I don't just stare at my inbox.

First day at the new job tomorrow. I've laid out my clothes, packed lunch, checked the bus times twice. Still can't sit still. What do people even say at the coffee machine? Tell me I'll be okay. Tell me nobody remembers the new person's first awkward hello.

Thursday night. The bake-off final is at ten tomorrow and I can't sleep. I keep running through the timings for the choux in my head. What if the oven at the venue runs hot? I've set three alarms. Stomach in knots already.

Sunday, 11 pm. Tomorrow I finally ask my manager about the promotion. I've practised the opening line in the mirror about forty times. My heart's going like the clappers just writing this down. Early bed. Probably won't help.

She did it. A whole length of the pool, no float, no hand under her tummy. She's beaming at me from the deep end, goggles crooked, and I want to stand on the bench and tell every parent here that the tiny one in the pink cap is mine.

Look at those courgettes. Three months ago this was a patch of weeds and broken bricks, and now there's a proper vegetable bed that I built myself. Sawed the planks, mixed the soil, everything. I keep stepping back to admire it. Yeah. I did that.

Replaced the cracked screen on my phone myself. Forty tiny screws, a video tutorial, and one very long evening, and it actually works. Touch, camera, everything. The shop wanted ninety quid. I'm going to show this to anyone who stands still long enough.

Distinction. I read it three times to be sure. All those nights at the kitchen table with flashcards while everyone else was out, and my tutor writing needs more work in every margin. Well. Not anymore. I sit back and let it sink in, chest puffed right out.

Did you see him? Did you see my son take that catch? Right on the boundary, one hand, fell over and held on. That's my boy. He's been practising in the back garden every night for a month. I told him he'd get there. Look at him, look at him celebrating.

I just read your report, Leah, and honestly it's the best piece of work to come out of this team all year. When you started you couldn't open a pivot table. Now the director is asking who wrote it. I told her. I made sure she knew it was you.

Second place in the village show! For my marmalade! Forty years I've been making it, and finally somebody official says it's good. I'm putting the rosette on the fridge where everyone can see it. Go on, have a taste. Told you it was the best in the county.

Mum! I ran the whole 10k without stopping! 58 minutes! Six months ago I couldn't run for a bus. Got my medal round my neck and I'm not taking it off for the rest of the day, maybe the week. Sending you the photo now, put it on the family chat.

Team, quick note before the weekend. We shipped the app update two days early with zero bugs reported so far. Every one of you pulled extra weight this sprint, and the client noticed. I've told leadership exactly who made it happen. Drinks are on me Friday. Brilliant work, all of you.

Dad finally beat me at chess. It took him a whole year of playing online every night after dinner, and he's 71. He rang me up shouting about it. I've never heard him so chuffed, and honestly I'm chuffed for him too. What a stubborn, brilliant old man.

Monday. Finished my first knitted jumper. The sleeves are slightly different lengths, but I made every stitch of it myself, from a ball of wool to something I can actually wear. Wore it to work. Told three people. Would have told more.

Friday. Our under-elevens won the league. I've coached these kids since they couldn't kick in a straight line. Today they passed, they defended, they shook hands with the other team. Best season of my coaching life. I'm framing the team photo.

Clearing out my old desk drawer, I find the notebook from my first job. Pages of to-do lists, so careful and so worried about tiny things. Funny how none of those deadlines matter now. I wonder what I'm fussing over today that I'll barely remember in ten years.

Same train, same window seat I've taken for nine years. The station café has changed hands three times and the trees by the canal have grown taller. I think about who I was when I started this route, how sure I was of everything. I'm less sure now. Maybe that's fine.

Stirring the soup the way Dad does, slowly, always clockwise, I realise I picked up most of my habits from watching him rather than listening to him. He never explained much. He just did things the same way every time, and somehow it all stuck.

Pulling up the last of the bean plants, I think back over the whole season. The early frost, the slugs, the week of rain in June. Some things I planned worked, most didn't, and the best crop was the squash I planted on a whim. There's probably a lesson in that.

You know, looking back at our first year in this flat, we argued about everything. Curtains, the heating, whose turn it was for the bins. I think we were just learning how to live with somebody. It's quieter now. Not because we agree more, just because we know each other better.

I was thinking on the drive over about the season we got relegated. At the time it felt like the end of the world. But that was the year we actually started training properly and listening to each other. Strange how the worst season ended up being the one that made us.

It's odd, isn't it, scrolling back through these photos from uni. We look so young. I remember thinking I had to have my whole life worked out by twenty-five. I didn't, and nothing fell apart. I keep coming back to that whenever I start fretting about the next thing.

Found our old group chat from first year while clearing my phone. We were so dramatic about every assignment. Reading it now, I mostly notice how much we looked out for each other. Not sure I ever said thanks back then. So, thanks, I suppose. Five years late.

Hi Raj, I was going through the archive today and found the first project plan we ever wrote together. It was hopelessly ambitious. Half of it never happened, and the part that did turned into the whole business. Made me think about how little of it we actually planned. All the best, Sam.

Mum, just walked past the old primary school on my way back from the shops. They've painted the gates blue. I stood there a while thinking about the walks home with you and how long those afternoons felt back then. Life moves at a different speed now, doesn't it.

Sunday evening. Another year of this journal almost finished. Flicking back through it, the things I wrote in capitals in January barely register now, and the small days, a long walk, a phone call with my brother, are the ones I keep rereading.

Tuesday. Quiet day. Sat by the window with tea and thought about the move to this city, six years ago this week. I came for a job I don't even have anymore. Stayed for reasons I couldn't have predicted. Funny how a life gets built sideways.

Her flat is empty now, just the pale outline on the wall where her bookshelf stood. Tomorrow she flies to Melbourne and I won't be able to knock on her door on a rainy Tuesday anymore. I keep picking up my phone to text her about dinner, then putting it down.

The café on the corner has whitewash on the windows and a thank you for twelve years sign taped to the door. That was where I wrote my whole dissertation, where the owner knew my order. I stand there holding a coffee from somewhere else, and it tastes of nothing.

The phone reset itself overnight and the backup never ran. Four years of photos, gone. The video of my nephew's first steps, the trip to the coast, Gran's handwriting on that birthday card I snapped. I keep scrolling the empty gallery as if they'll come back. They won't.

His room is so tidy now. The bed's made, the posters are rolled up in a tube in the corner, and the house has gone very quiet. I set out three plates at dinner without thinking, then put one back in the cupboard. Term doesn't end until December.

So that's it, then. Last game. The club's folding at the end of the season and the pitch is being sold for flats. Fifteen years of Sunday mornings, and I don't know where any of us will go. Can we just sit here a bit longer before we pack up the nets?

I keep finding his things around the flat. A sock behind the radiator, his awful mug. We agreed it was the right call, and it was. It's just so quiet when I get in from work. I didn't know you could miss somebody's noise this much.

Grandad, I know you have to sell the house, and it makes sense, it's far too big for you now. But I grew up in that garden. Every summer, the swing, the plum tree. I'm going to miss it so much. Can we go round one more time before the keys go?

They cancelled the trip. All six of us had been saving since January and now the whole thing's off because of the flights. I'd already packed half my bag. I know it's only a holiday, but I was really looking forward to seeing everyone together. Just feel a bit empty tonight.

Hi Ana, I just saw the announcement that you're leaving at the end of the month. I don't really know what to say. You've been the best part of this job for five years. Mondays won't be the same without your terrible puns. The office is going to feel very empty.

The servers for our old game shut down tonight. Logged in one last time and walked round our guild hall with nobody else there. Eight years of Friday raids with people I've never met in person but talked to more than half my family. Just gone, like that.

Saturday. Gave my old bike to the charity shop today. It had been in the shed for years and I never ride it, but Dad taught me on that bike. Watched the man wheel it into the back room and had to sit in the car a while before I could drive home.

Thursday. Lily's last day at our school. Her family is moving up north for her mum's job. We swapped friendship bracelets at the gate and promised to video call every week. The desk next to mine is just empty now. Didn't feel like eating my tea.
